hot.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences
hot.summary: Researchers from UIUC and NYU propose Temporal Difference in Vision (TDV), a self-supervised method for learning visual representations from video by predicting future frame embeddings from past frames and learned motion. This approach, which avoids strong inductive biases, demonstrates improved performance on dense spatial tasks like optical flow and stereo depth compared to existing techniques like DINO and iBOT.

hot.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction
hot.summary: The Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington developed MolmoMotion, a system that forecasts object-attached 3D point trajectories in world coordinates, conditioned on language instructions and visual history. This method improved robot manipulation task success rates by over 20 percentage points and enhanced video generation realism, outperforming existing motion prediction baselines on a new 3D motion benchmark.

hot.title: VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models
hot.summary: VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion-parameter model from Sina Weibo Inc., achieves advanced verifiable reasoning capabilities, matching or exceeding the performance of significantly larger language models on demanding benchmarks in mathematics, coding, and scientific reasoning. The model scored 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, further improving to 97.1 on AIME26 and 99.2 on BruMO25 with Claim-Level Reliability Assessment.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotWorld introduces a language-conditioned video world model from the Qwen Team that unifies various embodied domains, including manipulation, driving, and navigation, using natural language as a singular action interface. The model predicts physically plausible future visual trajectories and demonstrates top performance on embodied intelligence benchmarks like EWMBench and DreamGen Bench.

hot.title: Looped World Models
hot.summary: LoopWM introduces the first looped transformer architecture for world modeling, leveraging iterative latent depth to achieve stable long-horizon simulations with high parameter efficiency. The model demonstrates superior predictive accuracy and reduced computational cost on benchmarks like ScienceWorld and AlfWorld, outperforming models up to 100 times larger.

hot.title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training
hot.summary: ExpRL, developed by researchers from Stanford University, Carnegie Mellon University, and OpenAI, introduces an on-policy reinforcement learning approach for mid-training large language models by using human-written reference solutions as dense reward scaffolds. This method improves the initial policy for subsequent sparse-reward RL, leading to enhanced reasoning capabilities and achieving 63.41% pass@1 on AIME-2026 after downstream training, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and sparse reward baselines.

hot.title: Latent Thought Flow: Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
hot.summary: Latent Thought Flow (LTF), developed by researchers at Singapore Management University and Ant Group, enables Large Language Models to perform adaptive, efficient multi-step reasoning directly within their continuous latent space. The framework, which leverages GFlowNets, achieved an average accuracy improvement of 9.5% and a 27.2% reduction in reasoning length compared to existing latent reasoning methods across various LLM backbones and benchmarks.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotManip, a Vision-Language-Action foundation model, demonstrates that aligning heterogeneous robotic data enables effective data scaling and emergent generalization capabilities for manipulation tasks. The model achieves robust performance across various out-of-distribution scenarios and real-world deployments by integrating a unified cross-embodiment formulation and a large-scale open-source pretraining corpus.

hot.title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
hot.summary: The Geometric Action Model (GAM) repurposes a pretrained Geometric Foundation Model (GFM) as a unified backbone for language-conditioned robot manipulation, integrating 3D perception, future geometry prediction, and action decoding. This approach improves policy robustness to environmental changes and achieves significantly faster inference speeds, up to 55 times quicker than diffusion-based baselines.

hot.title: DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model
hot.summary: The DreamX Team developed DreamX-World 1.0, a general-purpose interactive world model that transitions video generation from passive synthesis to dynamic, user-controlled simulation. This model achieved the highest overall scores in basic (84.76) and long-horizon (70.41) evaluations against larger competitors, and was preferred by humans in 57.5-61.9% of cases, while also demonstrating enhanced scene persistence and real-time streaming at up to 16 FPS.

hot.title: Variable-Width Transformers
Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
hot.summary: Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM), developed by researchers at ELLIS Institute Tübingen and ETH Zurich, present a looped transformer architecture designed for stable and adaptive reasoning. The model incorporates a fixed-point convergence mechanism for intrinsic halting and utilizes pre-normalization with residual scaling to manage signal propagation in deep effective layers, achieving competitive or superior performance on various puzzle tasks while adaptively allocating computation based on task complexity.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System
hot.summary: A scalable navigation model, Qwen-RobotNav, built upon Qwen3-VL, enables dynamic adaptation of visual stream consumption through a reconfigurable observation strategy. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse embodied navigation, question answering, and autonomous driving tasks while serving as a flexible component within agentic systems.

hot.title: Unified Multimodal Autoregressive Modeling with Shared Context-Visual Tokenizer is Key to Unification
hot.summary: UniAR, a unified autoregressive framework, integrates visual understanding, generation, and editing by employing a single discrete visual tokenizer with multi-level feature fusion and binary spherical quantization. This approach enables competitive performance across diverse multimodal tasks and fosters emergent interleaved generation-understanding within a shared context.

hot.title: From AGI to ASI
hot.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind establish an analytical framework to map the potential evolution of artificial intelligence from AGI to ASI, outlining four technological pathways and six specific bottlenecks. The work provides a research agenda for predicting and managing the development of advanced AI capabilities.

hot.title: GameCraft-Bench: Can Agents Build Playable Games End-to-End in a Real Game Engine?
hot.summary: GameCraft-Bench introduces a rigorous benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing coding agents' ability to generate complete, playable games end-to-end within a real game engine, revealing that top agents currently achieve only around 40% of desired functionality. The benchmark leverages Godot 4 and a multimodal judge to evaluate engine-grounded, fully constructed game artifacts based on replayed gameplay interactions.

hot.title: Learning from the Self-future: On-policy Self-distillation for dLLMs
hot.summary: d-OPSD introduces the first on-policy self-distillation framework tailored for diffusion large language models, leveraging 'self future-experience' and step-level divergence supervision to enable self-improvement. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in reasoning tasks while demonstrating superior sample efficiency, converging in approximately 10% of the optimization steps required by RLVR methods.

hot.title: A Semi-Analytical Loss Cone Theory for Tidal Disruption Event Rates Around Kerr Black Holes
hot.summary: This research from the University of Oxford establishes a semi-analytical framework for calculating tidal disruption event (TDE) rates around spinning black holes, integrating relativistic strong-field effects with stellar dynamics. The framework reveals a first-order bias towards the disruption of retrograde stars while demonstrating that the overall, inclination-integrated TDE rate remains largely insensitive to black hole spin (a second-order effect).

hot.title: EgoCS-400K: An Egocentric Gameplay Dataset for World Models
hot.summary: EgoCS-400K introduces a large-scale egocentric gameplay dataset comprising over 400,000 first-person videos and 10,000 hours of professional Counter-Strike gameplay, offering dense, temporally aligned annotations to support the development of interactive world models. This resource provides explicit control signals, internal game states, and event records synchronized with visual observations for agent-oriented learning.

MiniMax Sparse Attention
likes.summary: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) offers an efficient, blockwise sparse attention mechanism for large language models, significantly reducing computational cost for ultra-long contexts. It maintains model performance across diverse tasks while achieving notable speedups, such as a 14.2x prefill and 7.6x decoding speedup at 1M context on H800 GPUs, driven by a 28.4x reduction in attention FLOPs.

likes.title: Unsafe AI or Consolidated Power: AI’s False Dichotomy
EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
likes.summary: EUREKAGENT introduces an agent environment engineering paradigm that coordinates off-the-shelf LLM-based CLI agents for autonomous scientific discovery, emphasizing external environmental design over prescriptive workflows. The system achieved new state-of-the-art results across mathematics, kernel engineering, and machine learning tasks through structured permissions, artifacts, budgets, and human-in-the-loop interfaces.

likes.title: EvoArena: Tracking Memory Evolution for Robust LLM Agents in Dynamic Environments
likes.summary: A new benchmark, EvoArena, evaluates Large Language Model agents in persistently evolving environments, complemented by EvoMem, a patch-based memory system that tracks knowledge evolution through structured update histories. This approach enhances agent robustness, achieving an average 2.6% step-level and 3.7% chain-level improvement across dynamic and static tasks by preventing memory "state collapse" in continuously changing contexts.

likes.title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
likes.summary: World Tracing, developed by World Labs and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, presents a generative pixel-aligned multilayer 3D geometry representation. It reconstructs visible surfaces and completes occluded 3D geometry from 2D inputs, showing improved accuracy on visible surfaces and comprehensive geometry generation for objects, scenes, and dynamic content while supporting various downstream 3D applications.

likes.title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers from Nanjing University and Alibaba Group investigated the parameter updates of On-Policy Distillation (OPD), revealing that it induces small, sparse, and spectrally concentrated modifications to model weights, primarily affecting off-principal directions. These findings indicate that OPD's on-policy data distribution drives a localized "editing" style of parameter refinement, distinct from dense supervised approaches.

likes.title: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
likes.summary: HarnessX is a framework for building composable, adaptive, and evolvable AI agent harnesses that achieved an average absolute gain of +14.5% in agent performance across various configurations. It enables agents to systematically learn and improve their runtime interfaces from execution feedback, including co-evolving with the underlying language model to internalize new strategies.

likes.title: Can I Buy Your KV Cache?
likes.summary: Researchers from Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, introduced a "prefill CDN" model, demonstrating that reusing precomputed Key-Value caches for shared document prefixes in Large Language Models is token-exact. This approach achieved 9-50x compute cost savings for repeated document access, offering substantial efficiency gains for long-context applications.

likes.title: Agents-K1: Towards Agent-native Knowledge Orchestration
likes.summary: Agents-K1 introduces a unified pipeline to construct agent-native scientific knowledge graphs from raw documents at scale, creating Scholar-KG from 2.46 million papers. The system enhanced multi-hop scientific reasoning for LLMs, with GPT-5.2's rationale accuracy increasing from 41.8% to 66.3% on geoscience research questions, and employs a 4B-parameter extraction model performing comparably to larger LLMs.

likes.title: RepWAM: World Action Modeling with Representation Visual-Action Tokenizers
likes.summary: RepWAM introduces a representation-centric World Action Model that employs a novel visual-action tokenizer (RepViTok) to create semantically rich latent spaces for robot control. It demonstrated improved success rates in real-world manipulation, achieving up to 80% on 'Push the drawer', and outperformed baselines in simulation benchmarks.

likes.title: Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA: From Vision-Language-Action Models to a Real-World Robot Learning Stack
likes.summary: HyVLA-0.5, a comprehensive robot learning stack from Tencent Robotics X and Tencent Hy Team, unifies high-fidelity data collection, VLM-based training, preference-driven policy refinement, and real-world deployment for generalist robots. The system achieved 90.9% success on clean simulated tasks and demonstrated effective cross-embodiment transfer and robust policy improvement via reward-free post-training on real robots.

likes.title: MaxProof: Scaling Mathematical Proof with Generative-Verifier RL and Population-Level Test-Time Scaling
likes.summary: MiniMax developed MaxProof, a framework that significantly improves large language models' capabilities in generating competition-level mathematical proofs. This is achieved by integrating a multi-stage trained M3 model, which can generate, verify, and refine proofs, with a population-level test-time scaling method that iteratively evolves and selects solutions. MaxProof enabled the M3 model to surpass human gold-medal thresholds on IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026, boosting its one-shot scores by 8 and 10 points, respectively.

likes.title: SpatialClaw: Rethinking Action Interface for Agentic Spatial Reasoning
likes.summary: SpatialClaw is a training-free framework for agentic spatial reasoning that enhances vision-language models by treating code as an iterative orchestration space for perception tools and scientific libraries. It enables dynamic sequencing and composition of tools, resulting in improved performance on a wide array of 3D and 4D spatial reasoning benchmarks.

likes.title: MaskWAM: Unifying Mask Prompting and Prediction for World-Action Models
likes.summary: MaskWAM introduces an end-to-end world-action model that enhances robotic control by integrating future mask prediction with visual prompting. The approach achieves improved policy generalization and resolves referential ambiguity by providing explicit semantic grounding and precise spatial anchoring across diverse manipulation tasks.
